newsitem.title: UK: British watchdog upholds complaint over Benetton advert.
newsitem.headline: British watchdog upholds complaint over Benetton advert.

text.p: Britain's main advertising watchdog said on Wednesday it had upheld a complaint about an advertising campaign by the British agent of Italy's retail giant Benetton SpA for one of its mountain bikes.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said it received a complaint from a consumer about an advertisement that showed in its top half a photo of a man standing in front of tanks during the Tiananmen Square demonstration in China in 1989 and the slogan 'Play Life'.
The bottom half, headlined 'Play Revolution' featured a picture of a mountain bike sold by Kastle UK, a division of Nordica SpA -- part of Benetton Sportsystem Communication.
The complainant noted that the man featured in the photo had been later executed for his actions and objected that "the use of the image for commercial purposes was offensive".
The ASA upheld this objection and said the photograph had no relevance to the product.
The ASA's ruling, published in its latest monthly report, is likely to be seen as the latest example of Benetton's controversial approach to advertising.
Recent ads for its clothes brand, several of which have been banned, included images of a new-born baby, an AIDS victim and a black horse mounting a white horse.
